headline: APPLETON FAULT STRIKES AGAIN: Rocky Shore Discovers Bulk Gold Zone 400m×600m in Newfoundland — Drill Program Tripled to 12,500m
snippet: Rocky Shore Gold Ltd. (CSE: RSG) announced June 10 that its initial reconnaissance drilling at the Lane Pond Gold Target within the Gold Anchor Project in central Newfoundland has returned a near-surface bulk-style gold zone intersected in eight widely spaced holes over 400 metres of strike and 600 metres down-dip — all associated with the prolific Appleton Fault structural corridor that hosts New Found Gold's landmark discovery northeast of the property. Management immediately expanded the program from 3,500 metres to 12,500 metres, with 13 holes complete, three reported, and the full dataset pending; the zone remains open in all directions.

headline: CANADA'S HISTORIC GOLD GIANT GOES BLUE CHIP: Hemlo's 25-Million-Oz Mine Graduates from TSXV to TSX Effective Monday June 15
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. (TSXV: HMMC) announced June 10 that it has received final TSX approval to graduate from the TSX Venture Exchange to the Toronto Stock Exchange, with common shares trading on the TSX under the same symbol 'HMMC' beginning Monday, June 15, 2026 — delisting from the TSXV at close on June 12. The Hemlo Gold Mine in northwestern Ontario has produced approximately 25 million ounces since 1985, making this one of the most significant exchange upgrades of the 2026 mining cycle; TSX graduation opens the company to index-tracking funds and a broader institutional investor base that the TSXV rules out.

headline: JAMES BAY LITHIUM EXPANDS: Brunswick Drills 27.4m at 1.13% Li2O, 350m×600m Anatacau System Open — High-Grade Cesium Confirmed
snippet: Brunswick Exploration Inc. (TSXV: BRW) reported June 10 final assay results from its 2026 winter drilling campaign at the Anatacau Main Project in James Bay, Quebec — seven holes totalling over 1,800 metres — confirming that the Anais Main dyke has been continuously intersected over a 350-metre-by-600-metre footprint open in all directions, with hole AN-26-12 returning 1.13% Li2O over 27.4 metres at shallow depth alongside elevated cesium and tantalum in surrounding zones. The 2026 winter results build the data foundation for a forthcoming maiden resource estimate, with the next drill campaign targeting Anatacau in late Q3 following a parallel program at the company's Mirage project.

headline: VISIBLE GOLD IN THE CALDERA: Scorpio Drills 6.95 g/t Au Over 11.98m Including 65.99 g/t Au, Phase 2 Now 92 Holes Deep in Nevada
snippet: Scorpio Gold Corp. (TSXV: SGN) released June 9 Phase Two drilling results from the Manhattan District Project in Nevada, with hole 26MN-091 returning 6.95 g/t gold over 11.98 metres from 242.99 metres depth within caldera volcanics at the Goldwedge target — including a visible-gold intercept of 65.99 g/t gold over 1.16 metres. Phase Two has now completed 92 holes for 25,919 metres with assays pending on 16 holes, and the discovery of new mineralization both inside and outside the existing Inferred Resource constraining pit signals system-scale growth potential that could reshape the resource boundary ahead of a planned resource update.

headline: TSXV DEBUT DELIVERS: Thistle Resources Reports 1.65 g/t Au Over 20.71m in New Brunswick's 7km Gold-Antimony System — Funded 2 Years
snippet: Thistle Resources Inc. (TSXV: TRCG), a recently listed junior explorer, reported June 10 certified NI 43-101 assay results for the Middle River Gold Project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp — the historically prolific base metal and gold district — with hole 21TRC-AU007 returning 1.65 g/t gold over 20.71 metres including 3.36 g/t gold over 7.82 metres. The project hosts a 7-kilometre gold system with ultra-high-grade antimony (a U.S.-designated critical mineral) and the company holds two years of exploration funding; the Bathurst Camp has seen renewed institutional interest as domestic antimony supply chains move up the priority list in 2026.

headline: $2 BILLION NPV AWAKENS: U.S. GoldMining Constructs Drill Pads at Whistler Alaska Gold-Copper Complex, DOE Power Study Advances Nearby
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ: USGO) reported June 9 that crews are actively constructing drill pads at high-priority targets within the Whistler–Raintree area of its 100%-owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project in Alaska, with the drill crew expected to mobilize in coming weeks and the 2026 program ahead of schedule and on budget. The update coincides with advancing district infrastructure catalysts: the proposed West Susitna Access Road and a DOE-funded $89M feasibility study for a 1.25-GW power plant 30 miles east of Whistler — both materially de-risking project economics relative to the existing PEA, which already outlines an after-tax NPV of $2.0 billion at $3,200/oz gold and $4.50/lb copper.

headline: UEC POWERS UP: $794M LIQUIDITY AND ZERO DEBT — Roughrider PFS Drilling 80% Complete as U.S. Uranium Sector Enters Summer Tightening
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE American: UEC) released Q3 fiscal 2026 results on June 9, reporting $794 million in liquid assets, no debt, and guidance for improved cost-per-pound and higher production in Q4 — against a backdrop of uranium spot prices near $85/lb as utilities sit on record uncovered future requirements. The quarterly results also confirmed that 80% of a planned 35,000-metre pre-feasibility study conversion drilling program at the world-class Roughrider Project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin has been completed, with Tetra Tech Canada engaged to lead technical services for the PFS — a de-risking milestone that could mark the next major re-rating catalyst for the stock.

headline: CATL'S STRANDED MINE ENDS LITHIUM'S BEAR MARKET: Jianxiawo Licence Still Frozen — CME Hydroxide Surges 86% YTD Back Above $20,000/t
snippet: A June 9 Mining.com column (republished globally) argues that the three-year lithium bear market has been broken not by a demand surge but by a single supply shock: Contemporary Amperex Technology's 150,000-tonne-per-year Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi province remains shut after its mining licence expired and CATL continues to wait for renewal — triggering a speculative buying wave that sent the CME lithium hydroxide contract 86% higher year-to-date to back above $20,000 per metric tonne for the first time since late 2023. The author cautions that most analysts expect a price correction once idled capacity re-enters the market, with BNP Paribas calling prices 'disconnected from fundamentals' and only Citi's $32,000/t upside target explicitly time-stamped to three months; for junior explorers and developers, the window of elevated pricing is real but potentially brief.

headline: $4,077 GOLD HOLDS CRITICAL SUPPORT: Strong US Payrolls Reinforce December Rate-Hike Bet — All Eyes on Warsh's June 17 FOMC Debut
snippet: Capital.com's June 10 technical analysis maps gold's slide to $4,077 — the new 2026 low — as the May US payrolls report (strong job creation) reinforced the market's December rate-hike pricing, compressing the non-yielding metal further even as the RSI fell to 23 (deeply oversold, the most compressed reading since March 2026). The piece identifies $4,050–$4,077 as the critical structural support zone where gold's bull market thesis either holds or faces a larger flush; with Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting and dot-plot release scheduled June 16–17, the next 6 days represent the highest-stakes macro window of the 2026 pullback — and the outcome will determine whether $4,000 is tested or whether the autumn rally gets an early start.

headline: HAMILTON: BUY JUNE DIPS IN GOLD — Summer Doldrums Are Seasonally the Best Entry Point; Autumn Rally Typically Launches by Mid-July
snippet: Adam Hamilton's annual 'Gold Summer Doldrums' analysis, published on GoldSeek in early June 2026, argues that the current selloff — with gold down 25%+ from January's $5,600 all-time high — is compressing into the seasonal weakness window that has historically preceded gold's strongest buying opportunities: June and early July weakness has consistently been followed by autumn rallies, with the mid-July period typically marking the inflection point. Hamilton notes that gold's entry into the doldrums in 2026 is happening from a less overbought position than past years (the January high was followed by rapid Iran-driven selloff rather than gradual distribution), which historically correlates with sharper and sooner recoveries — making current prices, while psychologically painful, a structurally attractive accumulation window for patient junior mining investors.
